title: HDFC Bank shares rebound from fresh 52-week low: What is driving the stock? - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
HDFC Bank shares hit another fresh 52-week low, second straight day, before trading at the day’s high in the mid-trading session on Thursday as the stock continued to remain in focus after investors weighed MD and CEO Jagdishan’s decision not to seek another term.

The stock traded at ₹693 at 12.22 pm on the NSE after touching a 52-week low of ₹686.20, down from the previous close of ₹687.10.

In the pre-open session, HDFC Bank shares remained firm at around ₹687.

The buy quantity incresed nearly 57 per cent to 17,90,214, and the sell quantity at 43 per cent to 13,49,387.

The traded volume of shares was 154.37 lakh, with a traded value of ₹1,063.17 crore.

The upper band and lower band were fixed at ₹755.80 and ₹618.40, respectively. The adjusted P/E ratio stood at 13.22.

HDFC Bank’s total market capitalisation stood at ₹10.66 lakh crore.

Over the week, the stock’s absolute returns fell 2.63 per cent. For the month, it declined 5.88 per cent, while YTD, it slumped 30.58 per cent.

Abhinav Tiwari, Sr. Research Analyst at Bonanza, remains positive on HDFC Bank and believes the recent weakness has created an attractive entry opportunity. He said concerns around CEO succession, Atanu Chakraborty’s resignation, Credit Suisse AT1 bonds, the ₹45 crore MSRDC arrangement and an ongoing US investor-related legal case have weighed on sentiment and valuations, but reviews and investigations have not indicated mala fide intent, personal enrichment or systemic governance failure.

Tiwari highlighted HDFC Bank’s around US$12 billion FCNR(B) deposits raised at 6.25 per cent and its current valuation of around 1.8x P/B, close to a multi-year low versus its historical range of above 2.5x P/B. He identified CEO succession clarity, resolution of the US legal case and NIM stabilisation as key triggers, and expects Kaizad Bharucha to take over as CEO for the next three-year term. According to Tiwari, the current valuation offers an attractive risk-reward, with most concerns viewed as transitional rather than structural.

“We believe the current valuation already discounts a significant portion of the negative news. The challenges following the HDFC Ltd merger are gradually being addressed, while the recent concerns have further depressed investor sentiment.”

“We see three key triggers: CEO succession clarity, resolution of the US legal case and NIM stabilisation. We expect Kaizad Bharucha to take over as CEO for the next three-year term, which should provide leadership continuity and improve investor confidence. Further improvement in deposits and normalisation of the credit-deposit ratio could provide additional support,” Tiwari said.

Virat Jagad, Sr. Technical Research Analyst at Bonanza, said HDFC Bank remains in a clear weekly downtrend, with the stock trading below major EMAs and facing rejection near ₹840. He noted that momentum remains weak, with ₹683 as the key support. Jagad advised avoiding fresh buying and said existing positions should be monitored closely, with ₹683–675 forming the major support zone. A breakdown below ₹683 could open the way towards ₹636–625.
